content: **Proposed 2026-09-09 by the LLM, and not part of the over-recall ruling: calibrate the non-match floor from the answerable side — a store's own queries — rather than from a probe set.** The argument was that the probe set had been the component to fail twice, that no store can hold a representative sample of what it will *not* be asked, and that the admissibility rule is stated on the answerable side anyway. **As first recorded it said a store already has such a history. It does not:** nothing records queries, and the 142 used in every floor measurement were recovered from session transcripts after the fact — see `floor-calibration-source`, which also holds the human partner's candidate sources. A shipped floor taken from real queries would want a margin below the observed minimum, since a minimum fitted to the queries seen so far will be undercut by a later one.
context: Settling the floor's operating point on 2026-09-09; split 2026-09-11 while returning to the Latin-script recall issue, when the human partner corrected the attribution.
why:
Split from `01M2369SVFEJGA5CKHA3KBQ23T` on 2026-09-11 UTC, after the human partner pointed out that this proposal had been recorded inside their ruling as though it were theirs. Kept separate so a later session does not lean on the human partner's authority for a claim that was mine.

Recorded at low confidence: its stated premise was wrong, and where the data would come from is exactly what `floor-calibration-source` leaves open. The argument against probe sets survives the correction; the claim that the alternative was ready to hand does not.

content: **The motivating gap is a bootstrap one, and it is the same gap `hoard-scope-topics` was invented to close** -- established when the question was raised, 2026-08-12. `keyword-standards` tells a session to use the spelling already in use, which requires a recall per candidate keyword, and for a set with no memories yet the question has no answer at all: there is no usage to consult, so the rule is silent exactly when a set's vocabulary is being established and the choices are most consequential. **Two constraints to settle if the feature is built.** A declared spelling must be **subordinate to the compiled `keyword-standards`** rather than able to contradict it -- a set could otherwise license a spelling the served rule forbids, and the served rule is the one a session is told to follow. And it is **another instruction-shaped channel arriving from a repository**, the same channel Trigger and Loading reasons about for conventions: much lower stakes than routing, since a bad spelling misfiles rather than misdirects, but the same shape and it should be reasoned about rather than waved through on the strength of being small.
context: Migrating open-questions.md into the memory set, when checking a cost figure in the charter-recall entry turned up a memory stored two entries earlier under a reserved keyword.
why:
Supersedes the original solely to correct a keyword. It carried the reserved mark `hoard-scope-topics` while being a memory *about* that mechanism rather than a charter, so it enrolled itself in the charter list and came back on the cross-set charter recall alongside the four real charters. The `about-` prefix is exactly the rule for this, and the failure it produces is the one `reserved-keywords-carry-subject-memories` records -- an issue marked fixed on the strength of the rule, which prevents new instances only if the rule is applied.

Recorded plainly because the instance is instructive: it was written on 2026-09-07 by a session that had loaded the corrected `keyword-standards` earlier the same day, and it was caught only because a later entry's cost measurement counted the charter recall's results. The rule does not fire on its own; something has to look.

content: Fixed 2026-08-25 by giving the pass its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` — `MUTATION_TARGET`, a sibling of `target/` rather than a child, set once in [scripts/mutate.py](scripts/mutate.py) at the single place commands are launched. The pass builds a binary no client is configured to run, so **the window closes at the root rather than being guarded**. Verified by watching `target/debug/scatterhoard` hold its timestamp through a pass that previously would have relinked it. **The silt moved with it, which is the second half of the win**: a pass leaves its files where nothing spawns from, so `rm -rf` is free at any time and the directory that wants clearing is no longer the one the servers depend on. The end-of-pass rebuild survives with a narrower job — keeping the mutation directory consistent with restored source — and its comment now records that it is no longer what protects a client.
context: Migrating ISSUES.md into the memory set, entry by entry.
why: A fix that removes the shared resource rather than guarding access to it, with a second benefit falling out: the directory that needs periodic clearing stops being the one live servers are spawned from.

content: **How to inspect a memory set without adopting it.** Raised 2026-08-26 by the human partner, from a maintainer reviewing a contributor's branch: import is adoption, and checking the branch back out does not undo it. **Designed in [load-modes.md](documents/design/load-modes.md) as a special case of read-only, which was built on 2026-09-17. Nothing now blocks building it.** Settled: an evaluation load comes from a file, once, through a `hoard_sets` action with no `create` step; several can be open at once; each is named `eval-<set>-<label>` with the label chosen by the user, and `SetName::new` refuses the `eval-` prefix; it is searched only when its scope is named; every memory it returns is marked from the load mode; it pulls no watch marks, drops without a safety copy, lives in memory, is never a holder of its source set's identity, and its recalls feed no floor calibration. Cross-set links out of it are surfaced with their target id, set name, identity and every loaded scope answering to that identity, and are never resolved; nothing resolves into it from outside. **Left as refinements, none of them blocking:** the size limit, to be set by timing a full embed; whether a returned memory carries its set's identity as well as the evaluation mark; and whether one recall can rank across two evaluation sets, which separate recalls do today with scores that are not comparable across calls. The findings accumulated under this question carry the keyword `evaluation-mode`; this record carries only its standing.
context: Designing evaluation mode: cross-set links, then calibration.
why: Supersedes the head because the last question named as *to settle before building* — calibration — is decided, so the entry's standing changed from blocked-on-decisions to ready. The three remaining items are refinements a first build can answer as it goes, and saying so is what stops the next session reading them as gates.

content: **The second benefit is the one that nearly went unbuilt, and it is worth more than the context saving that motivated the parameter.** Recorded in the design before the build and restated here 2026-09-07 on migration: `already_known` *lets a second call mean something other than what you just gave me, which is otherwise impossible against a deterministic ranking* — that is **stateless paging**. Pass back the ids already held, ask again, receive the next tranche: no cursor, no session state, nothing the server has to invalidate, which is what the design's own *per-call parameter, not session state* rule requires. Proved end to end 2026-08-18 in the recorded response `recall_already_known.json`. The human partner raised the same want independently on 2026-08-16 from the other direction — a way for the LLM to explore more broadly, cursoring through larger sets, partly as a recovery mechanism for an obscure memory. **What it does not reach**: paging recovers a memory ranked a little too low, not one ranked three hundredth, since sixty pages is not a recovery mechanism. The genuinely obscure memory is what keyword search and direct lookup exist for, and what traversal is now measured to reach.
context: Migrating the recall-already-known entry out of BACKLOG.md; this is the benefit the entry argued was underweighted.
why:
Recorded because the limit and the benefit are easy to confuse, and confusing them sends a session paging when it should be doing a keyword recall or a lookup. The parameter is a paging primitive that happens to save context, not a search-recovery mechanism — two callers wanting different things arrived at the same parameter, which is why the distinction has to be stated rather than inferred.

The statelessness is the part that will look like an omission: a cursor would be the conventional design, and this deliberately has none, so that there is nothing for the server to hold or invalidate between calls.

content: **The first independent negative class came from the human partner's own notes, because no corpus on this machine was off-domain for Scatterhoard's queries.** `coding-lessons` overlaps by subject and `governance-docs` by structure, so on 2026-09-09 the human partner supplied notes from a domain of their life that is neither. `corpus/harvest_questions.py` reads a notes vault and emits interrogative sentences only, dropping any that carry a proper noun, digit, address, identifier, software term or sensitive subject: 1,279 of 1,596 candidates were dropped, leaving 317. The questions themselves are not in the repository, and only aggregate counts appear in the memories.
context: The human partner offering notes from an unrelated volunteer role as a source of real off-domain questions, after every other source on the machine had turned out to overlap.
why: Where a negative class comes from decides what it can show. Anyone repeating the measurement needs to know that a same-machine corpus will overlap, and that the questions are private and stay out of the repository. Split out on 2026-10-18 from a memory restated during the publication review. The facts are unchanged.

content: **Four unifying explanations refuted on 2026-09-08/09, and the fourth closes the family: no surface feature of a query predicts its score.** (1) **`why` in the embedding input** — killed by its own control. (2) **Question form** — question-shaped nonsense reaches p90 0.192 against real off-domain 0.275. (3) **Word-level lexical overlap** — r² 0.100. (4) **Subword overlap**, run at the granularity the model actually uses (WordPiece over a Bert pre-tokenizer, 63091 tokens): **mean share r² 0.113, max share r² 0.012, rho 0.073.** The *max* statistic — the single-strongest-constituent theory that motivated the test — is the worst of all, because max is saturated by stopwords: `the` has 100% document frequency, `in` 84%, so question-shaped nonsense carries the highest max share of any family (0.9966) and the lowest score (0.150). **Two specific predictions failed outright**: `>` is only **4%** document frequency, so `>>> <<< ||| ~~~ ^^^` at 0.478 is not a frequency effect; and `stale`, at 10%, is worth 0.110 by minimal pair. **Frequency is the wrong weighting** — what matters is a token's direction, which is the embedding, which is where we started. Re-run `probe_whether_subword_overlap_predicts_the_score`.
context: Running the subword test agreed at the end of the long recall session, immediately after checkpointing and committing the rest. Split 2026-09-24 in step 2 of the out-link work, because the memory was over the length limit.
why: Supersedes the three-refutation record, which carried the subword test as its one outstanding caveat; that caveat is now discharged, and one coherent record beats a second half-record beside it. Superseded rather than amended because the original was exported and committed in `33866e3`. Confidence 0.9 on the refutations, which are direct measurements with named counter-examples. There is still no positive account, and none is claimed.

content: Found and fixed 2026-08-23, the same day. The guards added for `a-set-can-suppress-another-sets-memory` key on `target_set IS NULL`, which is correct for every case they were written for and wrong for one: a link naming its own set targets a memory in that set and should change its standing. **Not reachable through our own tool, which over-refused it for the mirror-image reason** — `cross_set_authority_refusal` asked *does this carry a set name* rather than *is the target in a different set* — but reachable by import, and a generator that always writes the set name explicitly would have produced nothing else. **The fix, in three parts**: `LinkTarget::is_foreign_to` asks the real question once, and both the refusal and the write use it; `write_memory` — the one place every write passes through, import included — stores a target naming its own set in the compact form, so the ambiguity never reaches the table; and `Store::compact_own_set_links` runs at open, because a store imported before the fix holds the long form and a set is not re-imported often enough for the write-side fix to reach it.
context: Migrating ISSUES.md into the memory set, entry by entry.
why: One question asked two wrong ways in two places — a guard testing for a set name's presence rather than for foreignness — with the fix funnelled through the single write every path shares, plus an open-time repair for stores already holding the bad spelling.

content:
**The human partner is prepared to raise the catalog budget for something important enough, and does not want the current headroom to constrain reasoning.** Stated 2026-09-12 while working out where a Golden Rule safeguard could live, with headroom at 322 characters of 18,000.

Their position has three parts, and the third is the operative one: they would raise the budget if needed; they believe there is still justification language that could be removed to make room; and **the order matters — establish whether a solution exists and what it costs, and only then decide whether it can be afforded.**

This is a stance rather than a decision. Nothing has been raised and no text has been identified for removal. It bears on `third-catalog-budget-raise`, which asks whether to raise the budget a third time and on what evidence: the evidence contemplated there was pressure from the catalog, and this is the human partner saying in advance that a sufficiently good clause is itself the evidence.
context: Reasoning about where a Golden Rule safeguard could live, when the remaining catalog headroom came up as a constraint.
why:
Filed against the budget entry because it is a stance on that question, arrived at from outside it — the kind of evidence that otherwise stays in whichever conversation produced it.

The ordering instruction is the substantive part and is easy to lose behind the willingness. A budget stated as fixed silently shapes what gets proposed, and a session that prices a design before knowing whether it works will discard the expensive-and-correct answer in favour of the cheap-and-partial one without ever saying that is what it did.

content: **Whether any label overrides uniform expansion. Resolved 2026-08-14: no.** The one candidate was `CONTRADICTS`, forcing both memories into the results so a contradiction cannot go unseen. **It needs no override, because the problem was visibility rather than promotion:** under the outbound rule the edge is written on the newer memory, so the older one -- likelier stale, and likely to surface on its own merits -- shows no trace of the dispute. Make the inbound edge visible and the caller decides whether the dispute bears on the work in hand, which is a judgement the software cannot make and the caller can. **It also scales better than forcing**, since supersession requires somebody to concede and cross-set disagreement leaves `CONTRADICTS` as the only instrument: visibility costs one identifier per dispute where a forced result slot would not. **The resolution was conditional on `incoming-edges-invisible-on-the-wire` being fixed with inbound edges on by default -- verified 2026-09-07, that issue is fixed, so the condition is met and the resolution stands unconditionally.** Whether a convention should tell the caller to follow up on a visible contradiction is deliberately left open. The findings accumulated under this question carry the keyword `label-overrides-uniform-expansion`; this record carries only its standing.
context: Migrating open-questions.md into the memory set, entry by entry in file order.
why:
Head of a question cluster: the question and its standing only. The opening sentence is the generated index row.

The condition is checked and reported in the head rather than carried across as a caveat, because a conditional resolution whose condition nobody re-checks is indistinguishable from an unconditional one -- and this one was genuinely contingent: had the inbound-edge defect stayed open, the answer *no override* would have left contradictions invisible, which is the failure the override existed to prevent.

*Visibility rather than promotion* is the reusable distinction, and it generalises past this label: the question for any proposed override is whether the caller lacks information or lacks a decision, and only the first is the software's to fix.

content: **Showing a lone memory beside up to four already-cleared memories from its subject cut `gemma4:12b`'s export-review misses from 8 to 6 in 144, and lenient quote matching removed the paraphrase false alarm.** Live on 2026-10-23 (`classify --final --context 4`, 3 runs). The husband at a mosque was now caught every time. The two remaining misses were the same memories in every run: an election campaign not read as politics, and "the person works at Northwind Bank" in a shared set, answered as about the project with nothing mentioned. There were 0 false alarms. The logs are in that session's scratchpad, `final-single-context`.
context: Testing the export review's per-memory questions on a small model before building, after the live run of the final approach found lone misses.
why: The residual misses are consistent on particular phrasings rather than scattered, so they look like the limit of what this model recognises, not carelessness that more context would fix. That makes accepting a residual risk on small models, stated plainly at the end of every review and backed by the strongest-model recommendation, the honest position. Context is still worth sending: it fixed one case and cost no false alarms.

content: Fixed 2026-08-20: `nested_reserved_directory` refuses a `directory` whose last segment is already `scatterhoard_mem`, naming what it recognised and telling the caller to pass the parent. Both `export` and `import` check it — import *before* it opens the file, because otherwise the failure reads as a missing `memories.json` and sends the caller looking for the wrong thing. **Refused rather than quietly corrected**: stripping the segment would be a guess, and wrong for anyone whose project root is genuinely named `scatterhoard_mem`, so the refusal names the remedy instead, per the standing rule that a message telling its reader to fix something must name an action its reader can take. The trailing-separator case is handled by comparing `Path::file_name` rather than the string, so `.../scatterhoard_mem` and `.../scatterhoard_mem/` are one directory to this check as to everything else; both are recorded mutations and both are caught. *The import test passed vacuously when first written* — import fails on the missing file anyway and that error quotes the path, so asserting the message merely mentions `scatterhoard_mem` proved nothing; it now asserts the guidance, and that the file was never reached.
context: Migrating ISSUES.md into the memory set, entry by entry.
why: The fix, with two things worth reusing: refusing rather than correcting where the correction would be a guess, and a vacuous test that passed because the unfixed path produced a message containing the same word.

Fixed 2026-09-06 by recognising an identity record structurally rather than by its keyword. The findings and measurements accumulated under this defect carry the keyword `about-hoard-author-as-a-subject-keyword-silently-disables-embedding`; this record carries only its standing.
context: Fixing genindex.py's positional slug pick, which turned up that this entry's slug began with the reserved prefix. Resuming from the 2026-09-21 checkpoint.
why: The head of an issue cluster under the tracking-files-as-index design: it holds the claim, the severity and the fixed-when, and nothing else. Superseded 2026-09-21 only to rename the slug: the old one began `hoard-`, which `keyword-standards` reserves for control marks and which `genindex.py` now skips when finding a head's slug, so the old spelling left this entry with no row. content: Both of the mutation runner's silt-up guards sat above the range where the cost appears, so neither fired while pace had drifted to twice its recorded healthy figure. Fixed 2026-08-09 by making them one conjunction that reports rather than asserts, recalibrated against a freshly cleaned tree. The findings accumulated under this defect carry the keyword `build-directory-alerts-only-catch-the-disaster`; this record carries only its standing.
